body.statement: Using the growing-component estimation handle, construct a concrete estimator from \(Z_1,\ldots,Z_n\) and derive an explicit \(T_n(\delta)\) such that \(\Pr\{E_{\mathrm{op}}>T_n(\delta)\}\le\delta\) when the number of centered Gaussian components is \(p+1\); characterize primitive weight, spectral-envelope, and pairwise-separation conditions under which \(T_n(\delta)<\varepsilon_{\star}\) with sample size polynomial in \(p\), and determine whether the perfect-surgery geometry weakens the near-disjoint total-variation separation required by generic centered-mixture clustering.
body.justification: This is the unresolved end-to-end statistical bottleneck rather than an assumed component-estimation oracle.
body.gap: Kumar et al. fix the component count, while Anderson et al. cluster growing centered mixtures under strong total-variation separation but do not deliver the surgery-specific operator-error tail consumed here.
body.consumer: A solution would turn the deterministic certificate into a growing-dimensional guarantee for genuinely pooled intervention samples.

obligation.what_is_open: Construct an explicit estimator of the unordered centered Gaussian component covariances for a growing number \(p+1\) of components and prove a permutation-matched operator-error tail \(T_n(\delta)\), together with primitive polynomial-sample conditions and a determination of whether perfect-surgery geometry reduces generic near-disjoint separation requirements.
obligation.obstruction: The frozen assumptions give only iid sampling, positivity of each weight, and population model membership. They impose no quantitative lower bound on mixture weights, no spectral upper envelope, and no pairwise component-separation margin. The qualitative handle in \(\texttt{def:mixture-estimation-handle}\) specifies neither a clustering algorithm nor a finite-sample theorem. Without those quantitative premises, rare components and arbitrarily close Gaussian components preclude a uniform growing-dimensional covariance tail.
obligation.attempted: The available route is projection followed by recursive clustering and effective-rank covariance concentration. Population characteristic-function separation proves identifiability but supplies no finite-sample cluster-label or covariance rate; generic Gaussian-mixture clustering bounds require explicit separation and weight assumptions absent from the frozen core. Perfect-surgery precision sparsity is useful only after sufficiently accurate component covariance recovery, and by itself has not been converted into a sample-level clustering separation bound.
obligation.partial_result:
The deterministic result already proves the following exact transfer.
For any concrete estimator satisfying
\[
 \Pr\!\left\{E_{\mathrm{op}}>T_n(\delta)\right\}\le\delta
\quad\text{and}\quad
T_n(\delta)<\varepsilon_\star,
\]
the event of any error in the recovered baseline, target bijection, or
DAG is contained in
\(\{E_{\mathrm{op}}>T_n(\delta)\}\), and therefore has probability at
most \(\delta\).  No explicit growing-\(p\) formula for \(T_n(\delta)\)
follows from the frozen assumptions alone.
